_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
Regions are reported in the source file's pixels, not the downscaled copy's: the conversation read a 3001x60 PNG, {{IMAGE}}, with read_image, which serves a downscaled copy. "The overlay" is ".image-comment-overlay"; "the frame" is ".image-comment-overlay .image-comment-frame" (it shrink-wraps the image, so its box is the image's displayed pixels and a fraction of it is a fraction of the image). "Drag from (a, b) to (c, d)" means: move the mouse over the frame at offsets (a × its width, b × its height) from its top-left, press the left button, move to (c × width, d × height) in N steps (5 unless said otherwise), and release; read the frame's box with getBoundingClientRect when computing the offsets. "Drag the middle half" is a drag from (0.25, 0.25) to (0.75, 0.75). The open comment dialog has its title ".diff-viewer-comment-dialog-handle" (it names the region being commented on), its input ".diff-viewer-comment-input" and its button "Add Comment" (name exactly that). window.geometry() returns the WxH+X+Y region the dialog title names; window.middleHalf(W, H) returns "ok" if that region is the middle half of a WxH image, within tolerance, and otherwise what is off; window.keepGeometry() keeps the current geometry for later, and window.kept(i) returns the i-th one kept (from 0). Check the message input's (data-testid "message-input") value with an eval comparing it to the exact string, building it with window.kept(i) where it says G or Gi; \n is a newline. Perform the steps in order.
1. Navigate to /c/image. Wait (up to 30s) for the first ".screenshot-tool .commentable-image" (the image) to be visible. 
2. The served copy really is downscaled, and did load; otherwise this test proves nothing (predictable's MaxImageDimension is 2000): the image's naturalWidth should come (within 15s) to be greater than 0, and should then be less than 3001.
3. Click the image. The overlay's ".image-comment-hint" should contain "Drag a box".
4. Drag the middle half. Reported in the 3001x60 source's pixels, not the rendered copy's: window.middleHalf(3001, 60) should return exactly "ok". Keep the geometry (G0).
5. Fill the dialog's input with "scaled correctly" and click "Add Comment". The message input's value should be exactly "> image {{IMAGE}} [region G0 of 3001x60]\nscaled correctly\n\n".

steps.expression: const r = document.querySelector('.image-comment-overlay .image-comment-frame').getBoundingClientRect(); window._drag = {sx: Math.round(r.width*0.25), sy: Math.round(r.height*0.25), ex: Math.round(r.width*0.75), ey: Math.round(r.height*0.75)}; `${window._drag.sx},${window._drag.sy} -> ${window._drag.ex},${window._drag.ey}`
